statement: A forward monotone path is a sequence of cells from (0,0) to (n-1,n-1) in which each step is either right or down and every cell has grid value 0 or 1. For any two such paths P and Q, let score(P,Q) be the number of distinct cells (i,j) that belong to P or Q and satisfy grid[i][j] = 1. The function returns a result r and r = max score(P,Q) over all ordered pairs (P,Q) of forward monotone paths when at least one forward monotone path exists; if no forward monotone path exists, r = 0.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). The input is an n x n grid (so every row has length n) with 1 <= n <= 50, every entry in {-1,0,1}, grid[0][0] != -1, and grid[n-1][n-1] != -1.

statement: For every grid satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r; it does not fail, overflow, panic, or access an out-of-bounds index.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). The input is an n x n grid (so every row has length n) with 1 <= n <= 50, every entry in {-1,0,1}, grid[0][0] != -1, and grid[n-1][n-1] != -1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 0 <= r <= min(C, 4n - 4), where C is the number of cells (i,j) with 0 <= i,j < n and grid[i][j] = 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). The input is an n x n grid (so every row has length n) with 1 <= n <= 50, every entry in {-1,0,1}, grid[0][0] != -1, and grid[n-1][n-1] != -1; additionally n >= 2.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = grid[0][0].
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). The input is an n x n grid (so every row has length n) with 1 <= n <= 50, every entry in {-1,0,1}, grid[0][0] != -1, and grid[n-1][n-1] != -1; additionally n = 1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every forward monotone path P from (0,0) to (n-1,n-1), r >= c(P), where c(P) is the number of cells of P with grid[i][j] = 1. A forward monotone path uses only right or down steps and only cells with grid value 0 or 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). The input is an n x n grid (so every row has length n) with 1 <= n <= 50, every entry in {-1,0,1}, grid[0][0] != -1, and grid[n-1][n-1] != -1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every ordered pair (P,Q) of forward monotone paths from (0,0) to (n-1,n-1), the number of distinct cells (i,j) that belong to P or Q and satisfy grid[i][j] = 1 is at most r.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). The input is an n x n grid (so every row has length n) with 1 <= n <= 50, every entry in {-1,0,1}, grid[0][0] != -1, and grid[n-1][n-1] != -1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exist forward monotone paths P and Q from (0,0) to (n-1,n-1) such that the number of distinct cells (i,j) that belong to P or Q and satisfy grid[i][j] = 1 equals r.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). The input is an n x n grid (so every row has length n) with 1 <= n <= 50, every entry in {-1,0,1}, grid[0][0] != -1, and grid[n-1][n-1] != -1; additionally there exists at least one forward monotone path from (0,0) to (n-1,n-1).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if there is no forward monotone path from (0,0) to (n-1,n-1), then r = 0.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). The input is an n x n grid (so every row has length n) with 1 <= n <= 50, every entry in {-1,0,1}, grid[0][0] != -1, and grid[n-1][n-1] != -1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if grid[i][j] != 1 for every 0 <= i,j < n, then r = 0.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). The input is an n x n grid (so every row has length n) with 1 <= n <= 50, every entry in {-1,0,1}, grid[0][0] != -1, and grid[n-1][n-1] != -1.

statement: Let gridT be the n x n grid defined by gridT[i][j] = grid[j][i] for 0 <= i,j < n. For every grid satisfying the preconditions, if r is the result returned by the function on grid and rT is the result returned by the function on gridT, then r = rT.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). The input is an n x n grid (so every row has length n) with 1 <= n <= 50, every entry in {-1,0,1}, grid[0][0] != -1, and grid[n-1][n-1] != -1.

statement: Whenever the function returns result rA on A and result rB on B, rB <= rA.
preconditions: Let A and B be two n x n grids with 1 <= n <= 50, every entry in {-1,0,1}, A[0][0] != -1, A[n-1][n-1] != -1, B[0][0] != -1, and B[n-1][n-1] != -1. Suppose B is obtained from A by changing zero or more cells with A[i][j] = 1 to B[i][j] = 0 and leaving every other cell unchanged.

statement: Whenever the function returns result rA on A and result rB on B, rA <= rB.
preconditions: Let A and B be two n x n grids with 1 <= n <= 50, every entry in {-1,0,1}, A[0][0] != -1, A[n-1][n-1] != -1, B[0][0] != -1, and B[n-1][n-1] != -1. Suppose B is obtained from A by changing zero or more cells with A[i][j] = -1 to B[i][j] = 0 and leaving every other cell unchanged.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 4n - 4.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). The input is an n x n grid (so every row has length n) with 1 <= n <= 50, every entry in {-1,0,1}, grid[0][0] != -1, and grid[n-1][n-1] != -1; additionally n >= 2 and grid[i][j] = 1 for every 0 <= i,j < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = c(P), where c(P) is the number of cells of P with grid[i][j] = 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). The input is an n x n grid (so every row has length n) with 1 <= n <= 50, every entry in {-1,0,1}, grid[0][0] != -1, and grid[n-1][n-1] != -1. Additionally, there is exactly one forward monotone path P from (0,0) to (n-1,n-1), where a forward monotone path uses only right or down steps and only cells with grid value 0 or 1.
